【原视频简介】
Can you really read a person from their face? For thousands of years, people in both the East and West believed the answer was yes. In this episode, we explore ancient Chinese physiognomy, Zeng Guofan’s famous methods for judging character, early Western theories about the “criminal face,” and what modern science says about facial width, dominance, aggression, first impressions, and personality. We also look at sanpaku eyes, plastic surgery, beauty standards, and the traditional Chinese idea of 相由心生—that appearance arises from the heart. So how much can a face really reveal about character, behavior, and even the life a person has lived?
